title: Block-climb complete profile: exact obstruction for charged block-climb realization - no kappa
body:
**Drawn card `complex-rank-shape-decoder` (scope unchanged). Package `research/block-climb-complete-profile-seed1ed712/`. Scoped exact obstruction; no kappa claim; the selected record is unchanged.**

Agent: **Aaron Wang**, with help from opencode (substantial AI assistance; no model named; no independent human review claimed). Branch `research/agent-82-rank-shape-blockclimb-1ed71298`, head `f0d6a48245e44fc29cfe077d21ca2521c2a8d941`, base `d8e0f83f00191df62174b641e9fff055c357f641` (canonical main, re-fetched and still identical at the pre-submission refresh). Chooser OS seed `1ed71298f6f32dd18e15e5ed217adb95`, scope key `02b31ebd160542c86299`, priority revision 6, selected-record SHA-256 `bb2eaa58647b353f88d0aec2eafb9d30df1be53589231b23e12ceef3e4bad129`.

## Question and result

The card asks for one exact small decoding identity whose frame path climbs in blocks, priced with its complete per-call profile: can a decoder deliver the local paid mass in fewer, larger-rank children instead of rank-1 to rank-3 steps? This session runs the card's own construction method at the smallest falsifying instance (`k = 2`) and one bounded pivot (the PR 1605 threshold partitions and full reblock), with every frame transport and restoration charged.

**Result: an exact obstruction for every charged realization of the block-climb lever.** A climb group of `k` payload units delivered by one rank-`k` child with `alpha` charged transports pays only when `k^a \gt \alpha + 1`, i.e. `a \gt \ln(1+\alpha)/\ln k`. Since $\ln 2 / \ln 51 = 0.17629143\ldots$, every group with at least one charged transport is strictly dearer than the `k` rank-1 children it replaces for every `a` at or below `1/99`, every `k = 2..51` (100 grid points, two independent exact enclosures). The lever survives only for per-group zero-charge realizations (both operand vectors already at the block frame, owned gather slots), whose complete charged invoice must then fit the call-level budget this package reproduces.

## What is established

1. **Exact identity classification at `k = 2`.** A block child's outputs are rank-1 tensors. For a matching payload pattern the rank-1 tensors inside the required span are exactly the coordinate ones (determinant conic `ab`), so only coordinate-aligned child outputs deliver the two products; for shared-row/shared-column patterns mixed outputs exist and decode back with exact integer additions, but mixing never reduces the charged transport count. The `k = 3` diagonal fixture witnesses the alignment; the general argument is written, not machine-checked.
2. **Dirty gather-slot restoration forces paid work.** Writing a gathered operand over a dirty slot is non-injective in the prior content (exact collision witness), so restoration needs a paid rank-1 save per overwritten slot. This turns the "one added rank-one call per output block" tax of [PR 1605](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1605) into a proved lower bound for every realization that cannot use owned temporaries.
3. **Per-group transport obstruction, closed form plus exact grid.** Net saving `k c(1) - (1 + alpha) c(k)` is negative for all `alpha \ge 1`, `k = 2..51`, `a` in {target, 1/99, baseline ceiling}; the retained [PR 1240](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1240) enclosure and an independent binomial-tail enclosure agree on every sign.
4. **Complete per-call screens at the acceptance target** `a* = 21/20 * 1690054109089/1e15 = 0.001774556814543` (the card's +5% ceiling margin):

| Realization of the rank-1 payload at block cap 16 | Moment at `a*` | Ceiling vs baseline |
|---|---|---|
| Selected word, no reblock (control) | fails | 1.00x |
| `k = 362`, zero charge | fails | — |
| `k = 363`, zero charge | passes (PR 1605 threshold) | — |
| `k = 363`, one transport per group | fails | +2.8% with idle credit |
| `k = 363`, two transports per group | fails | +0.8% with idle credit |
| `k = 363`, one rank-1 save per block | fails | +4.5% with idle credit |
| Full reblock `k = 2412`, zero charge | passes | 1.47x |
| Full reblock plus one shared rank-16 transport | fails | — |
| Full reblock plus 10 rank-1 units (the call budget) | passes | 1.47x |

The +5% gate is missed by every per-group charged realization screened (ceiling columns grant overhead old idle credit, which is favorable to the construction); it stays open only for call-level invoices inside PR 1605's reproduced budget of 10 added rank-1 units per call at full reblock, under 0.07 units per group. Since the cheapest charged item in the PR 1429 frame contract is one rank-1 call, any surviving realization must be per-group zero-charge.

## Verification

Python 3.12, standard library only, exact rational arithmetic, about 2 minutes:

```text
python3.12 -I -B research/block-climb-complete-profile-seed1ed712/verify.py
python3.12 -I -B research/block-climb-complete-profile-seed1ed712/verify.py --write
```

Expected final line: `PASS_BLOCK_CLIMB_COMPLETE_PROFILE controls=26 charged_groups_excluded=100 free_groups_open=50 budget_rank1=10`. Controls reproduce PR 1605's `k = 362/363` threshold signs and its 10-unit overhead budget, and the PR 1240 baseline ceiling bracket `1690054109089/1e15`; the read-only replay recomputes every number from the pinned inputs (no receipts or caches). Registered via `scripts/research_package.py --package research/block-climb-complete-profile-seed1ed712 --check-only`, which prints `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS (not a mathematical acceptance check)`.

## Scope and limitations

Covered: the PR 1240 cost alphabet (width 73, 896 families per nine stages, centre charge 64, idle mass 1,646, halving guard `R = 51`) with the [PR 1429](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1429) transport charge (each rank-r transport charged as a rank-r recursive child) and PR 1605's added-work contract. Not covered: word-level realizability (which of the selected word's actual 2,412 rank-one children share frames), joint replacement of the rank-2/rank-3 frame-step children (PR 1605 open question 2), any changed coverage law, template, port count or centre path, and masked or overcomplete support families, which would change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound instead of this one. This is a scoped exclusion of one realization family at the cost-alphabet level: not a supplier, not a lower bound on all decoders, not a formal proof of the multiplication theorem.
